newsitem.title: MEXICO: Serfin builds huge reserves for bank unit.
newsitem.headline: Serfin builds huge reserves for bank unit.

text.p: Grupo Financiero Serfin went on a reserve-building spree for its stricken bank unit Banca Serfin in 1996, causing a gaping net loss of 7.446 billion pesos, compared with a 22 million peso profit in 1995.

In a statement, Serfin said the bank created reserves of 2.9 billion pesos during Q4 and 8.335 billion pesos for the year. Its Q4 loss was 2.868 billion pesos, much wider than the 205 million peso drain in the last quarter of 1995.
The reserve building cut into its capitalization ratio that measures risk-based capital over risk-based assets, Serfin said.
The ratio fell 1.8 percentage points to 10.5 percent from the previous quarter.

"The decline in the capitalization level is a direct result of the provisions created during the quarter. Banca Serfin considers the actual levels adequate considering that the remaining 34 percent of the recapitalization plan should be completed during 1997," the statement said.

In the statement of results, Serfin made no mention of the long-awaited sale of a 19.9 percent stake to a unit of suitor HSBC Holdings Plc. Analysts had expected both announcements to be made simultaneously.
Later, however, Serfin chairman Adrian Sada said a sale could be announced this week.

Unexpectedly, the banking group announced the complex sale of 10.3 billion pesos of mortgage loans to Bank Insurance Fund Fobaproa, in exchange for a 10-year note issued by Fobaproa. The government had previously said it would do no more to bail out Mexico's banks, which have required billions of dollars in support since the 1994-5 economic crisis.
But Serfin said the move was aimed at supporting its sale efforts.

Including its mortgage sales to Fobaproa, Serfin issued a breakdown of its asset quality levels according to international accounting standards, or U.S. GAAP, saying that as of Feb. 28, its past-due loan ratio as a percentage of total loans more than doubled to 22.6 percent.

Its reserve coverage ratio over past due loans was 59.4 percent, down from 123.4 percent under Mexico's old accounting standards but comfortably above the 40 percent required by law. Meanwhile, allowances as a percentage of total loans under GAAP rose to 13.4 percent from 11.7 percent.

On the operating side, Serfin reported a slew of losses, counteracted only by a rise in net interest income in the fourth quarter to 1.039 billion pesos, up 258 million pesos from the previous quarter. In the year, it rose 666 million pesos.
The rise was due to an improved funding mix, a more stable and liquid money market and a higher yield on earning assets, Serfin said.

On the downside, non-interest income fell 304 million pesos in the fourth quarter to 307 million pesos, foreign exchange income dropped to 86 million pesos from 206 million in the previous quarter and its net trading result registered a loss of 67 million pesos. Serfin said its brokerage subsidiary Operadora de Bolsa Serfin reported net income of 35 million pesos in Q4, bringing 1996 profits to 155 million.

Seperately, Serfin noted that as of Feb. 17, Guillermo Quiroz was named the group's chief financial officer. He is the former CFO of Cintra SA de CV, the holding company of Mexicana and Aeromexico airlines.
